Maria: Quick request — can someone run a focused latency/variance scan for the new delta-7b model? We saw good median numbers in the preflight but some apps reported tail spikes. Target SLO: p95 < 120ms for common prompt set, p99 < 300ms if possible. Can we run a canary on pool-dedicated-3 with the following knobs:

- quant: int4-smooth
- tiling: auto (but capture fallback counts)
- batch sizes: 1,2,4,8 (no batching >8)
- kv mode: slice-kv enabled
- run at two seq lengths: 128 and 512

Also capture GPU perf counters (SM%, HBM BW) and kernel fallback logs. Please post a quick summary and any artifacts. Thanks.

Jamal: Taking this. Will run the canary now on pool-dedicated-3. Using bench-runner v2.3 with the delta-7b:v1 image. I’ll capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and OOMs/fallbacks. ETA ~ 25m.

perf-bot: canary deployment started: model=delta-7b:v1 target_pool=pool-dedicated-3 run_id=canary-2553219876-1

Sanjay: Heads-up — if you see p99 spikes, look at tiling fallback metric (runtime.tiling.fallback_count). We saw similar with orca-variants where fallback -> expensive single-kernel path. Also enable kernel_trace for a short window.

Jamal: Quick smoke results (seq=128): p50=38ms, p95=110ms, p99=420ms, tokens/sec=1150 (batch=1). Fallback_count=22 over 5k requests. Notable spikes at ~p99 correspond to fallback events. No OOMs at batch<=4, batch=8 caused transient OOM on one machine. Full logs uploading.

Alex: Re: OOM — that usually indicates fragmentation combined with slice-kv overhead on older driver. Which CUDA driver on pool-dedicated-3? If it's 525.x we see more fragmentation. Two quick mitigations: drop batch=8 from canary, or enable `runtime.allocator.compact_on_free=true` (cheap to flip).

Jamal: Driver is 525.85. Enabled compact_on_free for second run and re-ran batch=8 (short). Result: batch=8 median 72ms, p95 210ms, p99 510ms, but no OOMs. Fallback_count dropped to 5 after kernel/quant tuning.

Sanjay: Uploading profiling snippet (sampling 1s window around a p99 spike):

```
# flame summary (top frames)
runtime::attention_tile_kernel       46%
runtime::kv_cache_eviction           18%
runtime::fallback_single_kernel     26%
other                               10%
```

Looks like fallback_single_kernel equals large latency contributor. We should check tiling heuristics for seq=128.

Maria: Nice. Can we try sequence=512 too? Especially interested in p95/p99 for longer contexts. If fallback rate scales with seq length we may need a tiling threshold change.

Jamal: Seq=512 run completed: batch=1 p50=140ms, p95=430ms, p99=1.2s, tokens/sec ~540. Fallback_count=88 over 2k requests. High fallback ratio. I've attached raw perf counters (SM 78%, HBM 92% at spike).

Alex: That p99 is concerning. Two follow-ups: (1) add a canary variant with `tiling.force=true` to force tiled path and compare, (2) add a quantization micro-tweak: try int4-smooth+remap table (small perf delta sometimes avoids fallback). I can submit the kernel flag change to runtime config if you want.

perf-bot: canary run completed: run_id=canary-2553219876-1 status=completed artifacts=gs://redwood-perf/canaries/2553219876/delta7b_v1/

Lei: Please publish a short onboarding note in the model registry: include summary numbers for seq 128/512, highlight p99 spike and the mitigation (compact_on_free + kernel flag). Mark model status = experimental until tiling heuristics tuned. I can do the doc if someone adds final numbers and a short artifact list.

Maria: I'll add the summary comments and data links to the onboarding doc later today. Next action items:
- Alex: propose tiling heuristic tweak + config PR (assign by EOD)
- Jamal: run forced-tiling canary and attach comparative numbers (tomorrow)
- Sanjay: dig into fallback kernel path and see if we can reduce its p99 cost (profiling follow-up)

Alex: On it. Will open PR #3124 with tests.

Jamal: Will run the forced-tiling canary tomorrow morning and drop results here.

Maria: Awesome, thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Alex reacted with :thumbsup: to Maria's last message.
